en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kakkārupupphapūjaka Bandhujīvakavagga 4 The Apadāna of the Elder Kakkārupupphapūjaka: "I was a merchant in Benares, and I made my living by trade. At that time, the Buddha Kassapa had passed away into Nibbāna. When I heard that the relics of the Teacher were being enshrined, I took a kakkāru flower and went to the place where they were. Having paid homage to the relics of the Teacher, I offered that flower. Because of that merit, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. For eighty-four thousand aeons I lived in the world of the gods; for eighty-four thousand aeons I lived as a human being. In every birth, I possessed great wealth and was a lord of men. I was always handsome, fair-skinned, and pleasing to behold. I was always wealthy, possessing abundant grain and many treasures. I was always a king, a sovereign over the four continents. Now I have attained the supreme state, the unsurpassed Nibbāna. I am a disciple of the Buddha Gotama, one who has reached the end of suffering."
having taken up a kakkāru flower.”
I offered it to the Buddha.
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
And in the ninth aeon from now,
I was a king, the supreme among beings;
a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Kakkārupupphapūjaka recited these verses.
This is the fourth legend of the elder Kakkārupupphapūjaka.
